items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: I think Howard wasn't able to make it one night, so he came up and you and Neely Bonds played together.

ctx.x: I don't know. You wouldn't try to play the same. You wouldn't try to play the same.

You wouldn't try to play the same. You wouldn't try to play the same. Like on high society, well, it'd be good. We'd make the same variation, but I'd make a second to it, you see. Piku had written out a second for me. And I don't know what happened to that clarinet. Because that was in Orlando, the band, too. So Piku was there, too? That was after something happened to his saxophone play. He got a regular job and he left the band. He took people in the band. Well, I heard you one night in Washington, in Germany,…
I think I... How would you describe Dick Allen's trombone play? Terrible. Yeah, that's right. Did you ever hear Neely Bonds in the old days play? Yeah, I see.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: How about Albert Burbank? Did you hear anything about him in the 20s?

ctx.x: Handy, oh Handy, yeah. Handy was good. His friends, yes. Now there's a couple more.

How about Albert Burbank? Did you hear anything about him in the 20s? Albert wasn't out. No. No. Albert wasn't young. Talk about it at all. He didn't play with bands that were... Well, I don't know no bands that were...
Well, I don't know no bands that were... Outside of the young bands when it started. Yeah, that's all I know.
